snapshot.title: 71st CARPHA Annual Health Research Conference — One Health
snapshot.whyThisHotel: Qualified prospect for selective accommodation and small ancillary hospitality, not the main conference venue. The announced meeting is on the SGU campus. Spice Island’s 64 luxury villa-style suites and all-inclusive beach-resort positioning suggest a possible fit for self-paying senior delegates, speakers or partner representatives whose travel policies allow it, plus optional pre/post stays. None of those segments is a confirmed booking. A small private dinner or reception is worth qualifying; the resort publishes wedding/event services for up to 35 guests, but that is not verified corporate meeting capacity. Do not assume the conference’s exhibition, catering or networking spend will move from campus to this hotel. Breakfast-only options merit discussion because delegates may spend conference days away from the resort.

Ask whether Roxanne Colthrust remains involved; use Veron Guy-Parks as an alternative administrative referral and Rhonda-Joy Lewis for routing if needed. Suggested positioning: “Could you direct us to the person coordinating accommodation for the 21–23 April 2027 conference? Do not claim preferred-hotel status, offer personal inducements, buy sponsorship on the assumption it secures room business, or displace the campus venue.

snapshot.title: Savor 10 Grenada — Full Circle 10th Anniversary Gala Dinner & Dance
snapshot.whyThisHotel: Qualified banquet-first prospect, not a confirmed open venue opportunity. Dinner, drinks, styling and dancing create genuine event demand, and the separate Local vibes offer explicitly welcomes Grenadians without a hotel stay. Spice Island Beach Resort's luxury beachfront setting, catering and event staff suit an intimate celebration or VIP chef's-table alternative. However, a full gala fit is conditional on attendance, dance-floor layout, nonresident access and an uncommitted venue requirement. Its official wedding page advertises up to 35 guests; an April 2026 meetings report describes St. Andrew's for up to 50 attendees, while a trade directory lists a 50-person banquet layout. These are different configurations, not proof of gala capacity with entertainment. The trip listing's group-size range of 1–100 is not booked attendance and must not be used as a banquet forecast.

snapshot.title: Kenwood Travel — Spice Island Beach Resort Weddings and Vow Renewals
snapshot.whyThisHotel: Strong product and destination fit for intimate luxury leisure celebrations on Grand Anse Beach, rather than assumed corporate or city-centre demand. Kenwood explicitly sells this resort for weddings and vow renewals and says it books the whole wedding party, including guests. The resort publishes wedding capacity of up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, on-resort planners and an all-inclusive honeymoon proposition. That 35-person figure is an event-capacity statement, not a room block or production forecast. Realistic pathway: UK couple enquiry → Kenwood wedding specialist qualifies dates, party and accommodation needs → resort confirms ceremony and suite availability → Kenwood confirms holiday bookings and introduces the in-resort coordinator → optional celebration enhancements are arranged. Additional guest accommodation and longer honeymoon stays are opportunities, not evidenced bookings.

Ask the Kenwood wedding team to route a supplier/account discussion to Janet Percy. Request confirmation of the current Grenada/Spice Island product and contracting owners, existing sourcing arrangement, wedding enquiry conversion and attributable accommodation production. With the resort’s account owner/coordinator, validate current packages, capacity and guest-booking workflow; then agree a targeted UK wedding/vow-renewal sales brief and enquiry-to-booking handoff. Use Manuela for approved campaign activation only after commercial readiness is confirmed. Open a dated group opportunity only on receipt of a specific party brief; link its rooms and wedding components to the same account/opportunity to prevent double counting.
